data.title: TDS Redirect Chain Depth Anomaly
data.description: Detects HTTP redirect chains (302, 301, or JavaScript-based redirects) exceeding a depth threshold where intermediate nodes are newly registered domains or have low reputation scores, indicating Traffic Distribution System (TDS) abuse. Legitimate web redirects rarely exceed 3 hops and typically traverse well-known CDN, analytics, or marketing infrastructure. TDS chains commonly use 4-7 or more hops through disposable intermediary domains to obfuscate the final destination, evade URL blocklists, and enable real-time traffic steering. Each hop in a TDS chain may perform user-agent filtering, geolocation checks, or bot detection before forwarding. This rule correlates redirect depth with domain age and reputation of intermediate nodes to distinguish malicious TDS chains from legitimate multi-hop redirects. Supports TP-0042 Phase 3 detection of TDS positioning and traffic funneling infrastructure.

enrichment_required.source: WHOIS enrichment (max domain age in redirect chain)
Reputation scoring enrichment (min reputation in redirect chain)

falsepositives: Advertising technology redirect chains through multiple ad exchanges
Affiliate marketing link chains with multiple tracking intermediaries
URL shortener services chained together by users
